say.t: Mist, the second day.
The boss received only two. The other four are gone from your computer too.
It put them away for me. Where, it didn't say.
Everything on the desk is where it was. The pager stays on 0.7734.
A zero-second voice note. You can open it; the bar runs to the end. Nothing.
Bzz.
I couldn't place this one. There's a table that reads it, inside the calculator lid.
You close your eyes. Something very light in your hand, plastic, with a click when it shuts.
The year you went abroad. The airport. Bought the day before leaving: your first phone, the number written on your palm.
Call when you land. Doesn't have to be long. Two rings and hang up, then I know you're there.
If the money runs short, say so.
It's enough.
The second year. The kitchen of the shared flat. Three laptops on the table: two PhDs and one master's.
Wang Lai was doing cognitive science. He talked without putting his chopsticks down.
What the lab here builds won't be usable back home for three years. Let's go back and build it ourselves.
You're the only one of the three of us who can write code.
Chen Weiwei was doing a PhD in management. Her slides were already done.
I've got the name: Weilai Intelligence. Easy to remember, right?
She wrote two characters on a napkin: 薇, 莱. Next to them, 未来 — the future.
Two characters. There was no third one on the napkin.
If you stayed, the offer you've got here is top tier. I know that.
On the technical side, you decide. All of it. I promise.
The two of us handle everything else. You just build.
Okay.
That night you called home. Two rings, hang up. They called back: two rings, hang up. You didn't say you were coming back.
A year later every phone in every hand had turned into a slab of glass. It still worked. Nobody called the number any more.
The one on the desk now is fifteen years later. "On the technical side, you decide" — nobody said it again in those fifteen years.
Today is over.
The last little box. A broken feature phone, a flip, one corner of the screen cracked.
It won't switch on. It doesn't need to.

items.text: Go to the screen and read the messages.

say.t: Wang got two of them. They come on Friday; team-building first, I set the toast times.
I put the four away. Do the team-building schedule first.

say.t: Replied.

Three diagrams, posted to the group.

Talk to the one in the corner.
